record.original_question: Can the McKay correspondence be generalized to more general groups and group schemes, including positive-dimensional algebraic groups, abelian varieties, non-reduced finite group schemes, and profinite groups?

evidence.quote: Problem 10.2. Generalize the McKay correspondence to more general groups/group schemes such as algebraic groups (of positive dimension), abelian varieties, non-reduced finite group schemes, and pro-finite groups.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The classical McKay correspondence relates, for a finite subgroup $G \subset \mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{C})$ acting on $\mathbb{C}^n$, the representation theory of $G$ (in particular, its nontrivial irreducible representations) with the geometry of a crepant resolution $Y 	o \mathbb{C}^n/G$ of the quotient singularity. In its derived form (after Bridgeland–King–Reid and others), it asserts an equivalence between the $G$-equivariant derived category $D^b_G(\mathbb{C}^n)$ and the derived category $D^b(Y)$ of a suitable crepant resolution (e.g.\ the $G$-Hilbert scheme), and on the level of $K$-theory/cohomology it matches irreducible $G$-representations with a basis of the cohomology of $Y$.

Formulate and establish an analogue of the McKay correspondence for actions of more general group objects on smooth varieties (or schemes), in each of the following settings:

1. Positive-dimensional linear algebraic groups $G$ acting on a smooth variety $X$ with good quotient $X/G$ having canonical/Gorenstein singularities, relating equivariant invariants of $(X,G)$ to invariants of a crepant (or suitable categorical) resolution of $X/G$.

2. Abelian varieties $A$ acting on smooth varieties (or appearing as group schemes of automorphisms of a variety), producing a correspondence between equivariant categories/cohomology for $A$ and invariants of an appropriate resolution of the quotient.

3. Non-reduced finite group schemes $G$ over a field of positive characteristic (e.g.\ infinitesimal group schemes such as $\mu_p$, $\alpha_p$) acting on a smooth scheme $X$, relating the representation theory of $G$ to the geometry of a resolution of $X/G$.

4. Profinite groups $G$ (with continuous actions, e.g.\ on a formal or pro-scheme), establishing a derived equivalence or cohomological correspondence between the equivariant derived category and the derived category of an appropriate (formal) crepant resolution.

In each case, identify the correct notion of crepant (categorical) resolution, formulate the precise statement of the correspondence (at the level of derived categories, $K$-theory, or cohomology), and prove it.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open-ended research program asking for extensions of the McKay correspondence beyond finite groups in $\mathrm{SL}_n$. Partial results exist (e.g., derived McKay correspondences for certain group schemes, motivic/equivariant versions, work in positive characteristic by Yasuda and others, and extensions to some non-reduced or infinitesimal group schemes), but a unified correspondence covering all the listed classes—positive-dimensional algebraic groups, abelian varieties, non-reduced finite group schemes, and profinite groups—is not established. The overall problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: The McKay correspondence for finite subgroup schemes
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work extending McKay-type correspondences to non-reduced/finite group schemes in positive characteristic, indicating only partial progress.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for non-reduced finite group schemes, but a general McKay correspondence in this setting is still being developed.

status_evidence.title: Yasuda - The wild McKay correspondence
status_evidence.snippet: Yasuda's wild McKay correspondence addresses positive-characteristic finite groups via motivic integration; extension to broader classes remains incomplete.
status_evidence.claim: Generalizations beyond tame finite groups are active and partial.
